sections.html:
Three county offices share the work, and all of them operate from the Administration Center at 729 Maple Street in Hillsboro. The Assessor puts a value on each parcel. The County Clerk staffs the first-level appeal board. The Collector mails the bills and receives the money.

  • Assessor: 636-797-5343 for real estate, 636-797-5466 for personal property, open weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.
  • County Clerk: 636-797-5478 to book a Board of Equalization hearing.
  • Collector: 636-797-5406, or write to P.O. Box 100, Hillsboro, MO 63050.

None of these offices sets your rate. School, fire, ambulance and other districts do that for the land inside their boundaries, so two houses in different school districts, say Fox C-6 and Hillsboro R-3, can have quite different totals.

The county lies south of St. Louis along the Mississippi River. Arnold is the largest city and Hillsboro is the seat; Festus, De Soto, Crystal City, Herculaneum and Pevely are among the other incorporated places. Population reached 233,132 in July 2025, with 96,228 housing units. Owners occupy 82.2% of homes, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $237,200.

With so many households owning, lenders pay a large share of the bills from escrow. If yours does, read the lender-request rule in the due date section below.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a home
sections.html:
The office uses mass appraisal: it takes the replacement cost of the buildings, subtracts depreciation, adds the land value and arrives at fair market value. Missouri has every parcel reassessed in odd-numbered years, and the next one is 2027.

Market value is then multiplied by the assessment level for the property class.

Assessment levels used in Jefferson County
Property classShare of market value taxed
Residential19%
Commercial32%
Agricultural12%

A bill can move even without a reassessment. Added improvements such as a garage or an extra acre raise assessed value, so does a finished house that had been prorated while under construction, and a voter-approved levy change shifts the total while value stays flat.

Real estate tax is due December 31 and becomes delinquent January 1. Bills appear on the county website in November and go out by mail late that month. When nothing has arrived by December 1, phone the Collector, since a missing bill is not an excuse for missing the deadline.

  • Pay at 729 Maple Street, online, or on the phone line at 1-877-289-0099. Debit and credit cards carry a 2.5% convenience fee with a $1.95 minimum, and an e-check costs $4.95.
  • Mailed payments need a postmark of December 31 or earlier, so find out when your post office makes its last pickup.
  • A mortgage company has to send the Collector a written request for each bill it intends to pay. A paper bill in your mailbox means the lender never asked for it.

The Collector cannot waive penalty or interest, a limit tied to section 139.100 and an Attorney General opinion. Under RSMo 140.100, land in the back tax book is charged an 18 percent penalty on each year's delinquency, and the penalty on land redeemed before sale cannot go above 2 percent per month.

Begin with a phone call to the Assessor. An appraiser will go over the value with you and look at whatever evidence you bring. If you still disagree, file with the Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. The filing cutoff is the second Monday in July each year, and the next one falls on July 12, 2027.

  1. Call the Assessor at 636-797-5343 and request an informal review.
  2. Call the County Clerk at 636-797-5478 for the forms and a hearing date.
  3. Bring five copies of any written evidence: one per board member, one for the board secretary and one for the Assessor.
  4. Watch for a certified letter with the decision, usually within 5 business days.
  5. If you are still unhappy, file a Complaint for Review of Assessment with the State Tax Commission and attach the board's letter.

The Commission deadline is September 30 or 30 days after the board's decision, whichever is later. Those 30 days run from the date on the letter. A property held by an LLC, trust, corporation or estate needs an attorney to file.

An open appeal does not delay the bill, so pay by December 31. To pay under protest, send full payment before the delinquency date along with a written statement of your grounds and the fair market value you claim. Writing the word protest on the check accomplishes nothing by itself.

Two programs apply here. The county runs a Real Property Tax Credit for Seniors, enacted February 15, 2024; ask the Assessor for details. The second is the state's Property Tax Credit Claim, which refunds part of the real estate tax or rent you paid during the year.

  • The state credit tops out at $1,100 for owners who live in the home and $750 for renters.
  • You may qualify at 65 by December 31 of the prior year, if you or your spouse are 100% disabled, or at 60 or older with surviving spouse benefits.
  • Household income, Social Security included, cannot exceed $30,000 for a single person or $34,000 for married homeowners.
  • File form MO-1040 with schedule MO-PTS, or form MO-PTC if you do not file an income tax return.

If a tornado, flood, fire or earthquake destroys your house, you can ask the Assessor to remove the residential value pro rata under section 137.082. Use the Destroyed Residential Property form.

At most closings the seller's share of the year's tax is credited on the settlement statement, and the buyer takes on the whole year's bill. Your settlement statement or title company shows the actual split.

A new deed recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office is what changes the owner in the Assessor's file. Names on real estate bills change only through a recorded deed, so a phone call alone will not update the owner or the mailing address.

  1. Ask the Collector for the amount due on every year, penalty and interest included, before you accept an offer.
  2. Give that figure to the title company so it can pay the balance from your proceeds.
  3. Confirm that your lender's escrow, if you have one, covers the current bill so it is not paid twice.

A cash sale follows the same path. The buyer's funds go through title, the delinquent years are paid first, and you keep what is left. Repairs and a lender's appraisal do not hold up the tax payoff.

faqs.q: By what date must a Jefferson County real estate bill be paid?
faqs.a: December 31 of the tax year. A payment postmarked later is charged penalty and interest, and the Collector cannot waive either one.

faqs.q: When is the Jefferson County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The Board of Equalization takes filings until the second Monday in July. Missouri reassesses in odd-numbered years, so the next notices arrive in 2027 with a July 12, 2027 filing date.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Jefferson County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Call the Collector at 636-797-5406. Owners should call if nothing shows up by December 1, and the December 31 deadline stays the same either way.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage lender pay the Jefferson County bill?
faqs.a: Only if it sent the Collector a written request for your bill. If the paper bill came to you, the lender did not ask for it, so ask the lender where it wants the bill sent.

faqs.q: Who pays the year's tax when I sell my Jefferson County house?
faqs.a: Usually the seller's portion is credited at closing and the buyer owes the whole year's bill. Your settlement statement lays out the split.
